messages:
Elaine: Postmortem doc for the late-night deploy outage is live: https://go.redwood/internal/postmortems/late-night-deploy-2026 — short summary below, please read the doc when you have a sec. :wave:

Elaine: TL;DR — Canary throttling + aggressive KV cache expiry caused a wave of cache misses -> request amplification -> increased tail latency and some 5xxs for ~30m (23:12–23:42 PST). Impacted hosted API and a few Dedicated pools.

Elaine: Key consequences: ~6–9% error rate spike for some tokens, increased p99 from 320ms -> ~1.2s, customer-facing retries surfaced. No data exfiltration.

deploy-bot: [23:09] Canary rollout started for service:model-servingsvc v3.2.4 -> 12 instances. Preflight health checks passed.

Elaine: Root cause summary (high level):
- Canary autoscaler logic allowed concurrent canary batches beyond intended limit when cache miss threshold spiked.
- Cache TTL configuration was accidentally lowered in the deploy (fast eviction), exacerbating miss amplification.
- Runtime backpressure didn't propagate quickly enough to the router, so retries accumulated.

Sahil: Adding owners for the high-priority fixes (from the doc):
- Action A: Revert TTL change in config and add a guarded feature-flag rollback (owner: @Sahil) — target: next 48h.
- Action B: Add a hard cap on concurrent canary instances to 5% and a preflight KV-smoke test (owner: @Jamie) — target: 1 week.
- Action C: Router backpressure hook to stop retries being forwarded under cache storm (owner: @Alan) — target: 2 weeks.

Jamie: Quick question — is the concurrent canary cap a runtime flag we can flip without redeploy?

Elaine: Yes, it will be a runtime flag in the orchestrator; Jamie will add a toggle and a graphite alarm. We want a manual kill-switch until the preflight is in place.

Alan: I’ll prototype the backpressure hook today. Plan: add a short-lived token bucket at the router that drops/queues excess when KV-miss rate > threshold.

Rachel: For customer comms — who’s drafting the post-incident note for affected Dedicated customers? I can take the first pass if someone gives me the rough impact numbers.

Elaine: Thanks, Rachel — I’ll pull the aggregated metrics and send you the dashboard snapshot. Use the one in the doc (section 3).

incidents-bot: [23:46] Follow-up meeting scheduled: Postmortem sync Thursday 09:30 PT in #incidents. Agenda: confirm owners, unblock deploy rollback path, test preflight.

Jamie: Noted. I flagged the deploy pipeline to block new canaries until we have the cap in place. :lock:

Sahil: Also proposing an automation: when cache miss rate spikes > X% for Y minutes, temporarily divert new requests to warm pool and scale slow. Will add proposal to the doc under "Prevention".

Elaine: Excellent — action owners, please update the doc with short checkboxes and expected completion dates. I'll mark follow-ups as blocking for the next release window if not done.

Rachel: Thanks all. I’ll draft the external note and post here for review before sending.

Alan: Will post a test plan once the router change PR is up.

Elaine: Appreciate the quick triage everyone — main doc link again: https://go.redwood/internal/postmortems/late-night-deploy-2026 — ping me directly for questions. :pray:
